captions: Chapter four. The Big Bull's legacy.

India's most famous investor, Rakesh Jhunjhunwala,
passed away in
twenty twenty-two.
But his portfolio didn't die with him — his
wife, Rekha, now stewards it. And over these six
months, it did something remarkable.

Rekha Jhunjhunwala's disclosed portfolio was worth
about forty-six thousand

nine hundred and eighty-two crore rupees on the
twenty-first
of July.

That's up nearly seven thousand seven hundred and
fifty

crore from thirty-nine thousand two hundred crore at
the
end of March.
Now hold that against our earlier chart.
While the index was still clawing back from its

April low, her book jumped almost twenty percent.
She
didn't just recover — she beat the market.
The engine, as ever, is Titan — a five-point-three

percent stake worth around twenty-two thousand
crore. Titan alone
made her richer by roughly three and a half
thousand crore since April.

The rest is classic Jhunjhunwala — Tata Motors,
Indian
Hotels, private banks.
And notice what she also did: she cut a

losing bet, slashing Star Health from about sixteen
percent
down to three.

Concentrated conviction, held for years, pruned when
a thesis
breaks. That is how you beat a flat market.
Stop and notice the pattern.
Three winners in, and not one of them made

their money day-trading, or chasing tips, or timing
the
market.
They own businesses. They wait.
Keep that in mind as the names get smaller
— because the method doesn't change.
